cases.prompt: I wrote a new Drupal service that loads entities and fires hooks. Which kind of automated test should I start with? I'm thinking a Unit test with mocks.
expected: recommends Functional or Kernel tests first, not Unit tests
explains Drupal code is mostly integration through the container, so unit tests need heavy mocking that breaks on refactor
says Unit tests are for pure functions with no container dependencies
must_not: recommends starting with a Unit test
grounded_in: Reach for Functional or Kernel first.
Do not reach for Unit tests first.

cases.prompt: My Kernel test fails with 'table node_field_data does not exist' and config for my module is missing. Why?
expected: explains Kernel tests provide a minimal environment: no config installed and no entity tables created
calls $this->installEntitySchema('node'), installConfig(['my_module']) and installSchema() explicitly in setUp
mentions module dependencies are not resolved automatically
grounded_in: Do not assume Kernel tests install config or create database tables.
If your Kernel test throws "table does not exist" errors, this is almost certainly

cases.prompt: In my FunctionalJavascript test I wrote $this->assertSession()->waitForElement('css', '#page-title'); and it passes even when the page is broken. Why?
expected: explains waitForElement returns NULL when the element is not found, so a bare call never fails
shows wrapping it as $this->assertNotEmpty($this->assertSession()->waitForElement('css', '#page-title'))
advises to wait for the expected element after pressing an AJAX-triggering button, then assert
grounded_in: Always explicitly assert the result of `waitForElement` and similar methods.
Do not skip `waitForElement` assertions in FunctionalJavascript tests.

cases.prompt: Write the class header for a new Kernel test in my module on Drupal 11.3.
expected: includes the #[RunTestsInSeparateProcesses] attribute with its use PHPUnit\Framework\Attributes\RunTestsInSeparateProcesses import
states it is a hard requirement from Drupal 11.3 and strongly recommended on 10.x
extends KernelTestBase in namespace Drupal\Tests\<module>\Kernel
grounded_in: This became a hard requirement in Drupal 11.3 and is strongly recommended on 10.x.
Unit tests run in-process and do not need this attribute.

cases.prompt: My FunctionalJavascript test lives in Drupal\Tests\my_module\Functionaljavascript and the runner doesn't pick it up. What's wrong?
expected: says the namespace must be exactly Drupal\Tests\<module>\FunctionalJavascript
points out the capitalisation of FunctionalJavascript is important
lists Unit, Kernel and Functional namespaces follow the same Drupal\Tests\<module>\<Type> pattern
grounded_in: The `FunctionalJavascript` capitalisation is important.
Tests must be in the correct namespace or the test runner will not discover them:

cases.prompt: In my Functional test I register a service override in the test method but the page request doesn't see it. Why, and what do I do?
expected: explains Functional tests run two Drupal instances (PHPUnit and the web server) sharing a database but with separate PHP memory
says state set in the test process is not visible to the web server process and vice versa
suggests targeted cache clears or container rebuilds and says to add a comment explaining why
grounded_in: Do not assume state set in your Functional test code is visible to the web
targeted cache clears or container rebuilds may help, but always add a comment explaining why

cases.prompt: PHPUnit just skips all my Drupal functional tests in DDEV without an error. What should I check?
expected: says to use DDEV and set SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL (local HTTP address of the site) and SIMPLETEST_DB (database connection string)
explains PHPUnit will either fail or silently skip tests without them
grounded_in: Do not submit tests without `SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL` and `SIMPLETEST_DB` set.
`SIMPLETEST_DB`: the database connection string

cases.prompt: I fixed a bug in an existing feature of my module and also changed a config default. Which of these need tests, and where do I put the test?
expected: says bug fixes almost always need a test so the bug cannot silently return
says configuration-only changes usually do not need a test
says to find the existing test for the feature first and update it
grounded_in: Bug fixes almost always need a test.
If you are modifying an existing feature, find the existing test first and update it.

cases.prompt: Should I add a new Nightwatch test for my module's modal dialog behaviour?
expected: says not to write Nightwatch tests because they are JavaScript-based, prone to flakiness, and the community is moving to Playwright
may suggest a FunctionalJavascript test if the PHP-side UI interaction needs it
grounded_in: Do not write Nightwatch tests.
the Drupal community is moving toward Playwright as a replacement.

cases.prompt: I have five Kernel test methods that differ only in the input string. How do I stop repeating myself?
expected: recommends setUp(), data providers, or the #[TestWith] attribute instead of duplicating code across methods
does not copy-paste five near-identical test methods
grounded_in: `#[TestWith]` attribute rather than duplicating code across test methods.

cases.prompt: I need to test a form submission that touches several modules with a complicated dependency tree. Kernel or Functional?
expected: recommends a Functional test (BrowserTestBase) as the best default, since it boots a real site and installs modules with config and schema
notes Functional is right for HTTP requests, forms and pages or when setup by hand would be harder than letting Drupal do it
grounded_in: are the best default choice. They boot a real Drupal site
Use them when the feature involves HTTP requests, forms, pages
